description: A password-gated browser SPA for sending inference requests through a Python 3.12 server-side proxy to an existing LLM endpoint.

services.name: Frontend
services.description: A plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript browser interface for password sign-in, prompt entry, and displaying non-streaming LLM responses. Conversation state and preferences remain in browser localStorage.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Provides type safety for the SPA and its API contract.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses plain JavaScript without compile-time type checking.

questions.rationale: The confirmed frontend must use plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

questions.question: Confirm the frontend implementation approach.

options.label: React
options.description: Recommended component-based SPA with strong support for async and streaming response interfaces.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive component framework for the SPA.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A compiler-based option with a smaller runtime.

options.label: Plain HTML
options.description: A minimal static interface without a component framework.

questions.rationale: The confirmed frontend is plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, served by FastAPI.

questions.question: Provide the upstream LLM endpoint contract.
questions.answer: Use a dummy non-streaming LLM endpoint for now. Load its URL and API key from server-side .env; do not expose either to the browser.
questions.rationale: The initial integration is a server-side proxy to a configurable dummy endpoint; the concrete request and response schema stays isolated in the proxy adapter.

services.name: Inference API Proxy
services.description: A Python 3.12 FastAPI service that validates the password-only login, keeps .env secrets server-side, proxies LLM requests, and serves the production SPA assets.

questions.question: Which language should the secure inference proxy use?

options.label: Python 3.12
options.description: Required runtime; compatible with FastAPI and modern async HTTP clients.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Uses Node.js for the proxy rather than the required Python 3.12 runtime.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Uses ASP.NET Core rather than the required Python 3.12 runtime.

questions.rationale: The application must run on Python 3.12.

questions.question: Confirm the backend implementation approach.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: Recommended: async Python 3.12 API framework with validation, automatic API documentation, and straightforward SPA static-file serving.

options.label: Flask
options.description: A lighter synchronous-first Python web framework.

options.label: Django
options.description: A full-featured Python framework with more built-in features than this proxy requires.

questions.rationale: The confirmed backend is Python 3.12 with FastAPI.

questions.question: Specify the password-login behavior.
questions.recommendedChoice: Shared password; persist valid browser sign-in locally
questions.answer: Use one password whose expected value is loaded from server-side .env. When a valid password is submitted, keep the browser signed in using localStorage until the user logs out or clears browser storage.
questions.rationale: This matches the confirmed password-only local sign-in behavior while keeping the expected password server-side.

questions.question: What data storage should the application use?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep conversations and preferences in browser localStorage; do not persist application data on the server.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Persist users, conversations, or structured application data server-side.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store uploads, documents, images, or other inference files.

options.label: Redis Cache
options.description: Keep transient server-side cache or session data.

questions.rationale: Prior requirements specify browser localStorage and no server-side datastore.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to use application features?

options.label: No
options.description: Make the inference interface available without an application login.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require the password-only application login before accessing inference features.

questions.rationale: Prior requirements specify a password-only login. Its password and all upstream endpoint secrets remain server-side in .env and are never exposed to the browser.
